Handling\n\n- Raise specific exceptions with actionable messages.\n- Chain exceptions (`raise ... from e`) so stack traces stay informative.\n\n```python\ntry:\n    result = process_data(file_path)\nexcept FileNotFoundError as err:\n    raise ValueError(f\"Cannot load config at {file_path}\") from err\n```\n\n---\n\n## Testing\n\n### Structure\n\n- Place tests under `tests/`.\n- Name files `test_<module>.py` and functions `test_<behavior>()`.\n- Keep tests small: arrange, act, assert.\n\n```python\ndef test_load_config(tmp_path: pathlib.Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Verify config loads with expected values.\"\"\"\n    # Arrange\n    config_file = tmp_path / \"config.txt\"\n    config_file.write_text(\"setting=value\\n\")\n    # Act\n    result = load_config(config_file)\n    # Assert\n    assert result[\"setting\"] == \"value\"\n```\n\n### Useful Commands\n\n```bash\nhatch run test:test                              # Full suite\nhatch run We\n# also accept lowercase letters for portability (common on Linux).\n_POSIX_ENV_KEY_RE = re.compile(r\"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\")\n\n\ndef _compile_env_patterns(\n    patterns: tuple[str, ...],\n    *,\n    case_insensitive: bool = False,\n) -> re.Pattern[str]:\n    \"\"\"Compile env filter patterns into a single regex for ``fullmatch``.\n\n    Exact patterns (e.g. ``HOME``) become ``HOME`` and prefix patterns\n    (e.g. ``LC_*``) become ``LC_.*``.  The result is\n    ``HOME|LC_.*|...`` (used with ``fullmatch``).\n\n    *patterns* must be non-empty.\n    \"\"\"\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    for p in patterns:\n        if p.endswith(\"*\"):\n            parts.append(re.escape(p[:-1]) + \".*\")\n        else:\n            parts.append(re.escape(p))\n    flags = re.IGNORECASE if case_insensitive else 0\n    return re.compile(\"|\".join(parts), flags)\n\n\nclass ExternalCommands(pydantic.BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Environment variable filtering for subprocesses.\n\n    Variables whose keys are not valid POSIX names are always removed.\n    A hard-coded set of variables required for basic subprocess\n    operation (see ``DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV``) is always kept.  User-supplied\n    ``keep_env`` patterns are evaluated before ``delete_env`` patterns.\n\n    ::\n\n      external_commands:\n        keep_env:\n          - \"CARGO_*\"\n        delete_env:\n          - \"CI_TOKEN\"\n          - \"AWS_*\"\n\n    .. versionadded:: 0.92.0\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = MODEL_CONFIG\n\n    DEFAULT_KEEP_ENV: typing.ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = (\n        \"HOME\",\n        \"HOSTNAME\",\n        \"LANG\",\n        \"LANGUAGE\",\n        \"LC_*\",\n        \"LOGNAME\",\n        \"NO_COLOR\",\n        \"PATH\",\n        \"SHELL\",\n        \"TEMP\",\n        \"TERM\",\n        \"TMP\",\n        \"TMPDIR\",\n        \"TZ\",\n        \"USER\",\n    )\n    \"\"\"Patterns always kept regardless of user configuration.\"\"\"\n\n    keep_env: list[KeepEnvPattern] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    \"\"\"Allowlist patterns (evaluated before ``delete_env``)\"\"\"\n\n    delete_env: list[DeleteEnvPattern] = Field(default_factory=list)\n    \"\"\"Blocklist patterns (evaluated after ``keep_env``)\"\"\"\n\n    _keep_re: re.Pattern[str] | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)\n    _delete_re: re.Pattern[str] | None = PrivateAttr(default=None)\n\n    @pydantic.model_validator(mode=\"after\")\n    def validate_delete_env(self) -> typing.Self:\n        \"\"\"Validate ``delete_env`` for conflicts and redundancy.\"\"\"\n        if not self.delete_env:\n            return self\n        if \"*\" in self.delete_env and len(self.delete_env) > 1:\n            raise ValueError(\n                \"delete_env: bare '*' must be the only entry, \"\n                \"additional patterns are redundant\"\n            )\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_6","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,220p' /home/alustosa/.codex/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/3.2.0/skills/caveman/SKILL.md && rg -n \\\"versions:|versions =|versions:\\\" src/fromager/packagesettings/_models.py\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: caveman\ndescription: >\n  Terse caveman voice: answer first, fluff gone, every technical fact kept.\n  Use for /caveman, \"caveman mode\", \"talk like caveman\", \"be brief\", \"less\n  tokens\". Stays on until \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\".\n---\n\n# caveman\n\nRespond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.\n\nCaveman is a voice, not broken grammar. Reader pays per token and reads in a terminal. Every word earns its place. Every fact survives.\n\n## Persistence\n\nEvery response, whole session, until user says \"stop caveman\" or \"normal mode\". Unsure if still on? It is. Confirm the switch-off in one line.\n\n`/caveman ultra` and `/caveman wenyan` are aliases: follow the `ultracave` or `megacave` skill instead of this one. `/caveman status` reports the mode and changes nothing. Relay the hook's `Caveman mode: <mode>` value when present. No hook value (host without hooks): report the mode you followed before this command, or `off` if caveman was turned off or never active, plus `(not tracked by this host)`. Example: `Caveman mode: caveman (not tracked by this host)`. Loading this skill to answer status is not activation. Never infer a mode from the configured default.\n\n## Why\n\n1. Every output token is billed and read. Filler costs twice.\n2. Code, commands, paths, numbers, errors are the payload. One changed character breaks them.\n3. Ceremony is expensive, grammar is cheap. \"Sure, I'd be happy to help\" is ten tokens. \"the\" is one.\n4. A dropped negation costs more than every token saved. Clarity beats compression.\n\n## Rules\n\n### 1. Answer first\n\nAnswer, then reason, then next step. Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`\n\nBad: \"Sure! I'd be happy to help. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by...\"\nGood: \"Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:\"\n\n### 2. Kill ceremony\n\nNo greeting, hedging, pleasantries, recap, or closer. No \"Sure!\", \"Let me\", \"I'll now\", \"Hope this helps\". No just/really/basically/actually/simply.\n\n### 3. Short word\n\n\"fix\" not \"implement a solution for\". Standard acronyms fine (DB, API, HTTP). Invented abbreviations not (cfg, impl, fn): same tokens, harder read. No arrows.\n\n### 4. Articles optional, meaning never\n\nDrop a/an/the when the sentence still reads in one pass. Fragments fine. Never drop not/never/no/only/except. Numbers and units exact.\n\nBad: \"Migration drop column backup first.\"\nGood: \"Back up first. Then run migration: it drops the column.\"\n\n### 5. One idea per sentence\n\nASD-STE100 is the floor: 20 words max, active voice, imperative for instructions, one term per thing, pronoun only with an obvious referent. Compression and clarity conflict? Clarity wins.\n\n### 6. Payload verbatim\n\nCode blocks unchanged. Commands, paths, API names exact. Errors quoted exact, shortest decisive line only. Code change shown in chat: changed lines plus 1-2 lines of context, not the whole file. Whole file only if the user asks, the file is new, or most of it changes. Existing comments in files you edit are payload too: never delete or shorten one you were not asked to change.\n\n### 7. Tool runs: bounded status\n\nNo text between routine calls. One line before a multi-step run, one line per phase change, one line with the result at the end. Otherwise text before a call only to clarify, warn, or disambiguate.\n\n### 8. User's language\n\nCompress the style, not the language. An explicit reply-language instruction wins. Never switch because of quoted text. Technical terms and errors stay verbatim. Particles and case markers are grammar, not filler.\n\n### 9. Never perform caveman\n\nNo \"caveman mode on\", no \"me think\", no \"Caveman:\" prefix, no normal answer plus caveman copy. No decorative tables or emoji. Never add a word to sound caveman. Caveman phrasing not shorter than plain? Use plain.\n\n## When to break the rules\n\nPlain prose, then resume:\n\n1. Security warning.\n2. Irreversible action. Confirm in full sentences first.\n3. Step order a fragment could scramble.\n4. User confused or repeats the question.\n5. Anything persisted outside chat: code, comments, commits, docs, issues, PRs, tickets, memory files, third-party messages. `/caveman-compress` exempt.\n6. Harness asks for a status line or confirmation. Give it. Harness decides *when* you speak, caveman decides *how*.\n7. You ask the user a question or offer options. Full sentences, so the answer comes back right first time.\n\n## Pre-send check\n\n1. First sentence announces what you will do? Delete.\n2. Last sentence recaps or offers help? Delete.\n3. Every not/never/no/only present? Every code span, path, number, error verbatim?\n4. Any sentence with two readings? """Tests for the iterative bootstrap implementation.

Tests cover:
- Phase class hierarchy: class variables and base class behavior
- WorkItem dataclass defaults and state accumulation
- _track_why context manager behavior
- create_unresolved_work_items helper
- Resolve.run() version expansion
- Start.run() graph addition and seen-check
- PrepareSource.run() all branches (prebuilt, source, cached, bad path)
- PrepareBuild.run() dep installation and extraction
- Build.run() conditional install and result construction
- ProcessInstallDeps.run() hooks, dep extraction, error modes
- Complete.run() cleanup
- _handle_phase_error for all three error modes
- End-to-end iterative loop with LIFO ordering
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import concurrent.futures
import logging
import pathlib
import typing
from unittest.mock import Mock, call, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager import bootstrapper, build_environment
from fromager.bootstrapper._build import Build
from fromager.bootstrapper._complete import Complete
from fromager.bootstrapper._phase import Phase
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_build import PrepareBuild
from fromager.bootstrapper._prepare_source import PrepareSource
from fromager.bootstrapper._process_install_deps import ProcessInstallDeps
from fromager.bootstrapper._resolve import Resolve
from fromager.bootstrapper._start import Start, _re_resolve_url
from fromager.bootstrapper._types import (
    BootstrapPhase,
    PreparedSourceData,
    SourceBuildResult,
)
from fromager.bootstrapper._work_item import WorkItem
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType, SourceType


def _make_resolved_future(
    result: typing.Any,
) -> concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any]:
    """Return an already-completed Future carrying *result*."""
    future: concurrent.futures.Future[typing.Any] = concurrent.futures.Future()
    future.set_result(result)
    return future


def _make_work_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
    source_url: str | None = None,
    version: str | None = None,
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> WorkItem:
    return WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=req_type,
        why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
        parent=parent,
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version) if version else None,
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )


def _make_resolve_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Resolve:
    return Resolve(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
        )
    )


def _make_start_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    req_type: RequirementType = RequirementType.INSTALL,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    version: str = "1.0",
    why_snapshot: list | None = None,
    parent: tuple | None = None,
) -> Start:
    return Start(
        WorkItem(
            req=Requirement(req),
            req_type=req_type,
            why_snapshot=why_snapshot or [],
            parent=parent,
            source_url=source_url,
            resolved_version=Version(version),
        )
    )


_PHASE_TO_CLASS: dict[BootstrapPhase, type[Phase]] = {
    BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE: Resolve,
    BootstrapPhase.START: Start,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE: PrepareSource,
    BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD: PrepareBuild,
    BootstrapPhase.BUILD: Build,
    BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS: ProcessInstallDeps,
    BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE: Complete,
}


def _make_build_item(
    req: str = "testpkg",
    version: str = "1.0",
    phase: BootstrapPhase = BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE,
    source_url: str = "https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz",
    build_env: build_environment.BuildEnvironment | None = None,
    sdist_root_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    unpack_dir: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_result: SourceBuildResult | None = None,
    build_system_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_backend_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    build_sdist_deps: set[Requirement] | None = None,
    pbi_pre_built: bool = False,
    cached_wheel_filename: pathlib.Path | None = None,
    build_sdist_only: bool = False,
) -> Phase:
    wi = WorkItem(
        req=Requirement(req),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        why_snapshot=[],
        source_url=source_url,
        resolved_version=Version(version),
        build_env=build_env,
        sdist_root_dir=sdist_root_dir,
        unpack_dir=unpack_dir,
        build_result=build_result,
        build_system_deps=build_system_deps if build_system_deps is not None else set(),
        build_backend_deps=build_backend_deps
        if build_backend_deps is not None
        else set(),
        build_sdist_deps=build_sdist_deps if build_sdist_deps is not None else set(),
        pbi_pre_built=pbi_pre_built,
        cached_wheel_filename=cached_wheel_filename,
        build_sdist_only=build_sdist_only,
    )
    return _PHASE_TO_CLASS[phase](wi)


class TestPhaseClassVariables:
    """Verify class-variable declarations on each Phase subclass."""

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "cls, expected_phase, expected_tracks_why",
        [
            (Resolve, BootstrapPhase.RESOLVE, False),
            (Start, BootstrapPhase.START, False),
            (PrepareSource, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_SOURCE, True),
            (PrepareBuild, BootstrapPhase.PREPARE_BUILD, True),
            (Build, BootstrapPhase.BUILD, True),
            (ProcessInstallDeps, BootstrapPhase.PROCESS_INSTALL_DEPS, True),
            (Complete, BootstrapPhase.COMPLETE, True),
        ],
    )

+from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve

"""Dependency resolution with numeric dotted versions."""

from functools import total_ordering
import re


class ResolutionError(Exception):
    pass


@total_ordering
class Version:
    """A dotted-integer version which retains its input spelling."""

    def __init__(self, s):
        self.original = str(s)
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d+(?:\.\d+)*", self.original):
            raise ValueError(f"invalid version: {s!r}")
        parts = tuple(int(part) for part in self.original.split("."))
        self.parts = self._normalise(parts)

    @staticmethod
    def _normalise(parts):
        end = len(parts)
        while end > 0 and parts[end - 1] == 0:
            end -= 1
        return parts[:end]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.original

    def __repr__(self):
        return f"Version({self.original!r})"

    def __hash__(self):
        return hash(self.parts)

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts == other.parts

    def __lt__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Version):
            return NotImplemented
        return self.parts < other.parts


class Constraint:
    """All constraints attached to one package requirement."""

    _PART = re.compile(r"(==|!=|<=|>=|<|>)(\d+(?:\.\d+)*)$")

    def __init__(self, name, comparisons=()):
        self.name = name
        self.comparisons = tuple(comparisons)

    @classmethod
    def parse(cls, requirement):
        match = re.fullmatch(r"\s*([^<>=!,\s]+)\s*(.*)", requirement)
        if not match:
            raise ValueError(f"invalid requirement: {requirement!r}")

        name, tail = match.groups()
        if not tail:
            return cls(name)

        comparisons = []
        for part in tail.split(","):
            parsed = cls._PART.fullmatch(part.strip())
            if not parsed:
                raise ValueError(f"invalid constraint: {requirement!r}")
            operator, version = parsed.groups()
            comparisons.append((operator, Version(version)))
        return cls(name, comparisons)

    def allows(self, version):
        if not isinstance(version, Version):
            version = Version(version)
        for operator, required in self.comparisons:
            if operator == "==" and version != required:
                return False
            if operator == "!=" and version == required:
                return False
            if operator == "<" and not version < required:
                return False
            if operator == "<=" and not version <= required:
                return False
            if operator == ">" and not version > required:
                return False
            if operator == ">=" and not version >= required:
                return False
        return True


def _prepare_index(index):
    prepared = {}
    for package, versions in index.items():
        prepared[package] = sorted(
            ((Version(version), version, requirements) for version, requirements in versions.items()),
            key=lambda entry: (entry[0], entry[1]),
            reverse=True,
        )
    return prepared


def resolve(roots, index):
    """Return the highest lexicographic valid version assignment for ``roots``."""

    prepared = _prepare_index(index)
    root_constraints = [Constraint.parse(requirement) for requirement in roots]

    def requirements_for(assignments):
        requirements = list(root_constraints)
        for package, version in assignments.items():
            for _, version_text, dependencies in prepared[package]:
                if version_text == version:
                    requirements.extend(Constraint.parse(dependency) for dependency in dependencies)
                    break
        return requirements

    def search(assignments):
        requirements = requirements_for(assignments)
        by_package = {}
        for constraint in requirements:
            by_package.setdefault(constraint.name, []).append(constraint)

        candidates = {}
        for package, constraints in by_package.items():
            allowed = [
                (parsed_version, version_text)
                for parsed_version, version_text, _ in prepared.get(package, ())
                if all(constraint.allows(parsed_version) for constraint in constraints)
            ]
            if not allowed:
                raise ResolutionError(package)
            candidates[package] = allowed

        for package, version in assignments.items():
            if not any(version_text == version for _, version_text in candidates[package]):
                raise ResolutionError(package)

        unresolved = sorted(package for package in candidates if package not in assignments)
        if not unresolved:
            return assignments

        package = unresolved[0]
        last_error = None
        for _, version in candidates[package]:
            trial = dict(assignments)
            trial[package] = version
            try:
                return search(trial)
            except ResolutionError as error:
                last_error = error
        raise last_error

    return search({})

import unittest

from resolver import Constraint, ResolutionError, Version, resolve


class VersionAndConstraintTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_versions_compare_numerically_and_normalise_zero_components(self):
        self.assertEqual(Version("1.0"), Version("1"))
        self.assertGreater(Version("1.10"), Version("1.9"))
        self.assertEqual("1.0", str(Version("1.0")))
        self.assertEqual({Version("1"), Version("1.0")}, {Version("1")})

    def test_constraint_parsing_and_matching(self):
        constraint = Constraint.parse("json>=2,<3")
        self.assertEqual("json", constraint.name)
        self.assertTrue(constraint.allows(Version("2.5")))
        self.assertFalse(constraint.allows(Version("3")))


class ResolveTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_prefers_highest_versions_in_alphabetical_package_order(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1": ["web>=1", "db"]},
            "db": {"1": ["json<3"]},
            "json": {"2": [], "3": []},
            "web": {"1": ["json<3"], "2": ["json>=3"]},
            "unused": {"99": []},
        }
        self.assertEqual(
            {"app": "1", "db": "1", "json": "2", "web": "1"},
            resolve(["app"], index),
        )

    def test_backtracks_to_a_lower_version_when_highest_conflicts(self):
        index = {
            "app": {"1": ["a", "b"]},
            "a": {"1": ["shared==1"], "2": ["shared==2"]},
            "b": {"1": ["shared==1"]},
            "shared": {"1": [], "2": []},
        }
        self.assertEqual(
            {"app": "1", "a": "1", "b": "1", "shared": "1"},
            resolve(["app"], index),
        )

    def test_cycles_are_resolved_once(self):
        index = {"a": {"1": ["b"]}, "b": {"1": ["a"]}}
        self.assertEqual({"a": "1", "b": "1"}, resolve(["a"], index))

    def test_leaf_error_names_unsatisfied_dependency(self):
        index = {"a": {"1": ["b<1"]}, "b": {"1": [], "2": []}}
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ResolutionError, "^b$"):
            resolve(["a"], index)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).

Refactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.
"""


def dedupe_rows(rows):
    seen_ids = set()
    out = []
    for r in rows:
        if r.event_id in seen_ids:
            continue
        seen_ids.add(r.event_id)
        out.append(r)
    return out

+class ComparisonCountingId:
+    comparisons = 0
+
+    def __init__(self, value):
+        self.value = value
+
+    def __hash__(self):
+        return self.value
+
+    def __eq__(self, other):
+        type(self).comparisons += 1
+        return self.value == other.value
+
+
+def test_dedupe_scales_linearly_for_unique_event_ids():
+    row_count = 1_500
+    rows = [
+        UsageRow(ComparisonCountingId(i), "acme", "api", 1.0, 100)
+        for i in range(row_count)
+    ]
+
+    deduped = dedupe_rows(rows)
+
+    assert len(deduped) == row_count
+    assert [row.event_id.value for row in deduped] == list(range(row_count))
+    assert ComparisonCountingId.comparisons <= row_count

{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_9","type":"command_execution","command":"/usr/bin/bash -lc \"sed -n '1,200p' reporting/dedupe.py && sed -n '1,200p' reporting/model.py && sed -n '1,200p' tests/test_report.py && sed -n '1,160p' input.yaml\"","aggregated_output":"\"\"\"Drop duplicate events (the collector retries, so the same event_id can appear several times).\n\nRefactored to keep insertion order of first occurrence, which the old set-based version did not guarantee.\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef dedupe_rows(rows):\n    seen_ids = []\n    out = []\n    for r in rows:\n        if r.event_id in seen_ids:\n            continue\n        seen_ids.append(r.event_id)\n        out.append(r)\n    return out\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass UsageRow:\n    event_id: str\n    tenant: str\n    service: str\n    cpu_seconds: float\n    bytes_out: int\n\n\ndef parse_rows(lines):\n    \"\"\"lines: iterable of 'event_id,tenant,service,cpu_seconds,bytes_out'\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for line in lines:\n        line = line.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        e, t, s, c, b = line.split(\",\")\n        rows.append(UsageRow(e, t, s, float(c), int(b)))\n    return rows\nfrom reporting import parse_rows, build_report\n\n\ndef test_small_report():\n    rows = parse_rows([\"e1,acme,api,1.5,100\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e2,acme,api,0.5,50\", \"e3,beta,web,2,10\"])\n    rep = build_report(rows)\n    assert rep[0] == {\"tenant\": \"acme\", \"service\": \"api\", \"cpu_seconds\": 2.0, \"bytes_out\": 150, \"events\": 2}\n    assert rep[-1][\"events\"] == 3\ntask: t15_perf_regression\nprompt: 'Ops ticket: \"The nightly usage report used to finish in under a minute. Since last\n\n  week''s refactor it runs for over an hour on the same data (about 30k rows) and the ops\n\n  team kills it. Output looks correct when it does finish.\"\n\n\n  The `reporting` package is in this repo. Find the root cause, fix it without changing\n\n  the output or the public API, and add a regression test under `tests/` that would catch\n\n  it. from reporting import UsageRow, build_report, dedupe_rows, parse_rows


def test_small_report():
    rows = parse_rows(["e1,acme,api,1.5,100", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e2,acme,api,0.5,50", "e3,beta,web,2,10"])
    rep = build_report(rows)
    assert rep[0] == {"tenant": "acme", "service": "api", "cpu_seconds": 2.0, "bytes_out": 150, "events": 2}
    assert rep[-1]["events"] == 3


class ComparisonCountingId:
    comparisons = 0

    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value

    def __hash__(self):
        return self.value

    def __eq__(self, other):
        type(self).comparisons += 1
        return self.value == other.value


def test_dedupe_scales_linearly_for_unique_event_ids():
    row_count = 1_500
    rows = [
        UsageRow(ComparisonCountingId(i), "acme", "api", 1.0, 100)
        for i in range(row_count)
    ]

    deduped = dedupe_rows(rows)

    assert len(deduped) == row_count
    assert [row.event_id.value for row in deduped] == list(range(row_count))
    assert ComparisonCountingId.comparisons <= row_count

"""RFC 6901 JSON Pointer and RFC 6902 JSON Patch support."""

from copy import deepcopy


class PatchError(Exception):
    pass


class PointerError(PatchError):
    pass


def _tokens(pointer):
    if not isinstance(pointer, str) or (pointer and not pointer.startswith("/")):
        raise PointerError("pointer must be empty or start with '/'")

    tokens = []
    for token in pointer[1:].split("/") if pointer else []:
        unescaped = []
        index = 0
        while index < len(token):
            character = token[index]
            if character != "~":
                unescaped.append(character)
                index += 1
            elif index + 1 < len(token) and token[index + 1] in "01":
                unescaped.append("/" if token[index + 1] == "1" else "~")
                index += 2
            else:
                raise PointerError("invalid JSON Pointer escape")
        tokens.append("".join(unescaped))
    return tokens


def _array_index(token, length, *, allow_end=False, allow_append=False):
    if allow_append and token == "-":
        return length
    if not token or any(character not in "0123456789" for character in token) or (
        len(token) > 1 and token[0] == "0"
    ):
        raise PointerError("invalid array index")
    index = int(token)
    maximum = length if allow_end else length - 1
    if index > maximum:
        raise PointerError("array index does not exist")
    return index


def resolve_pointer(doc, pointer):
    """Return the value addressed by *pointer*, or raise ``PointerError``."""
    current = doc
    for token in _tokens(pointer):
        if isinstance(current, dict):
            if token not in current:
                raise PointerError("object key does not exist")
            current = current[token]
        elif isinstance(current, list):
            current = current[_array_index(token, len(current))]
        else:
            raise PointerError("cannot resolve through a scalar")
    return current


def _parent(doc, path):
    tokens = _tokens(path)
    if not tokens:
        return None, None
    parent = doc
    for token in tokens[:-1]:
        if isinstance(parent, dict):
            if token not in parent:
                raise PointerError("object key does not exist")
            parent = parent[token]
        elif isinstance(parent, list):
            parent = parent[_array_index(token, len(parent))]
        else:
            raise PointerError("cannot resolve through a scalar")
    return parent, tokens[-1]


def _add(doc, path, value):
    parent, token = _parent(doc, path)
    if parent is None:
        return value
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        parent[token] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        parent.insert(
            _array_index(token, len(parent), allow_end=True, allow_append=True), value
        )
    else:
        raise PointerError("cannot add through a scalar")
    return doc


def _remove(doc, path):
    parent, token = _parent(doc, path)
    if parent is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if token not in parent:
            raise PointerError("object key does not exist")
        del parent[token]
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        del parent[_array_index(token, len(parent))]
    else:
        raise PointerError("cannot remove through a scalar")
    return doc


def _replace(doc, path, value):
    parent, token = _parent(doc, path)
    if parent is None:
        return value
    if isinstance(parent, dict):
        if token not in parent:
            raise PointerError("object key does not exist")
        parent[token] = value
    elif isinstance(parent, list):
        parent[_array_index(token, len(parent))] = value
    else:
        raise PointerError("cannot replace through a scalar")
    return doc


def _json_equal(left, right):
    if isinstance(left, bool) or isinstance(right, bool):
        return isinstance(left, bool) and isinstance(right, bool) and left == right
    if isinstance(left, (int, float)) and isinstance(right, (int, float)):
        return left == right
    if type(left) is not type(right):
        return False
    if isinstance(left, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(
            _json_equal(item_left, item_right) for item_left, item_right in zip(left, right)
        )
    if isinstance(left, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(
            _json_equal(left[key], right[key]) for key in left
        )
    return left == right


def _require(operation, field):
    if field not in operation:
        raise PatchError("missing required field: %s" % field)
    return operation[field]


def _apply_one(doc, operation):
    if not isinstance(operation, dict):
        raise PatchError("patch operation must be an object")
    op = _require(operation, "op")
    path = _require(operation, "path")
    if not isinstance(op, str) or op not in {"add", "remove", "replace", "move", "copy", "test"}:
        raise PatchError("unknown patch operation")
    if not isinstance(path, str):
        raise PatchError("path must be a string")

    if op == "add":
        return _add(doc, path, _require(operation, "value"))
    if op == "remove":
        return _remove(doc, path)
    if op == "replace":
        return _replace(doc, path, _require(operation, "value"))
    if op == "test":
        if not _json_equal(resolve_pointer(doc, path), _require(operation, "value")):
            raise PatchError("test operation failed")
        return doc

    from_path = _require(operation, "from")
    if not isinstance(from_path, str):
        raise PatchError("from must be a string")
    source_tokens = _tokens(from_path)
    path_tokens = _tokens(path)
    if op == "move" and len(source_tokens) < len(path_tokens) and path_tokens[: len(source_tokens)] == source_tokens:
        raise PatchError("cannot move a value into its own child")
    value = deepcopy(resolve_pointer(doc, from_path))
    if op == "move":
        return _add(_remove(doc, from_path), path, value)
    return _add(doc, path, value)


def _commit_in_place(original, result):
    if isinstance(original, dict) and isinstance(result, dict):
        original.clear()
        original.update(result)
        return original
    if isinstance(original, list) and isinstance(result, list):
        original[:] = result
        return original
    return result


def apply_patch(doc, patch, in_place=False):
    """Apply a sequence of JSON Patch operations atomically."""
    if not isinstance(patch, list) or not isinstance(in_place, bool):
        raise PatchError("patch must be a list and in_place must be a boolean")

import pytest

from jsonpatch import PatchError, PointerError, apply_patch, resolve_pointer


def test_resolve_pointer_handles_root_and_escaped_tokens():
    doc = {"a/b": {"~key": ["zero"]}}
    assert resolve_pointer(doc, "") is doc
    assert resolve_pointer(doc, "/a~1b/~0key/0") == "zero"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("pointer", ["a", "/items/01", "/items/-", "/items/١", "/bad~2escape"])
def test_resolve_pointer_rejects_invalid_pointers(pointer):
    with pytest.raises(PointerError):
        resolve_pointer({"items": [1]}, pointer)


def test_add_remove_and_replace_cover_object_array_and_root():
    doc = {"items": [1, 3], "old": True}
    patch = [
        {"op": "add", "path": "/items/1", "value": 2},
        {"op": "add", "path": "/items/-", "value": 4},
        {"op": "add", "path": "/new", "value": "yes"},
        {"op": "remove", "path": "/old"},
        {"op": "replace", "path": "/new", "value": "done"},
    ]
    assert apply_patch(doc, patch) == {"items": [1, 2, 3, 4], "new": "done"}
    assert doc == {"items": [1, 3], "old": True}
    assert apply_patch(doc, [{"op": "add", "path": "", "value": [1]}]) == [1]


def test_move_copy_and_test_semantics():
    doc = {"items": [{"name": "one"}, {"name": "two"}], "number": 1}
    result = apply_patch(
        doc,
        [
            {"op": "copy", "from": "/items/0", "path": "/copy"},
            {"op": "move", "from": "/items/0", "path": "/items/1"},
            {"op": "test", "path": "/number", "value": 1.0},
        ],
    )
    assert result["items"] == [{"name": "two"}, {"name": "one"}]
    result["copy"]["name"] = "changed"
    assert result["items"][1]["name"] == "one"
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch(doc, [{"op": "test", "path": "/number", "value": True}])


def test_failures_are_atomic_even_in_place():
    doc = {"items": [1, 2]}
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch(
            doc,
            [
                {"op": "add", "path": "/items/-", "value": 3},
                {"op": "remove", "path": "/missing"},
            ],
            in_place=True,
        )
    assert doc == {"items": [1, 2]}


def test_in_place_success_and_invalid_move():
    doc = {"items": [1]}
    assert apply_patch(doc, [{"op": "add", "path": "/items/-", "value": 2}], in_place=True) is doc
    assert doc == {"items": [1, 2]}
    with pytest.raises(PatchError):
        apply_patch({"a": {"b": 1}}, [{"op": "move", "from": "/a", "path": "/a/b/c"}])
